title: Flat simplicial modules are unchanged in homology by a quasi-isomorphic change of simplicial rings
statement:
Let $R_\bullet,S_\bullet:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CRing}$ be simplicial commutative rings and $f:R_\bullet\to S_\bullet$ a morphism [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. A simplicial $R_\bullet$-module $M_\bullet$ means a simplicial abelian group with an $R_n$-module structure on $M_n$ for every $n$, such that for every $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ the operator $M(\varphi):M_n\to M_m$ satisfies $M(\varphi)(rx)=R(\varphi)(r)M(\varphi)(x)$. Suppose that each $M_n$ is flat over $R_n$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For a simplicial abelian group $N_\bullet$ put $s(N)^{-n}=N_n$ for $n\geq0$, with differential $\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^id_i$ from degree $-n$ to $-n+1$ for $n\geq1$, and zero terms in positive degrees. Suppose that $s(f):s(R_\bullet)\to s(S_\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Form the simplicial $S_\bullet$-module $M_\bullet\otimes_{R_\bullet}S_\bullet$ degreewise [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with operator $x\otimes y\mapsto M(\varphi)(x)\otimes S(\varphi)(y)$. Then the canonical map
$$s(M_\bullet)\longrightarrow s(M_\bullet\otimes_{R_\bullet}S_\bullet),\qquad x\longmapsto x\otimes1,$$
is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of abelian groups.

source.place: Tag 08RX (lemma-O-homology-qis), specialized to the category Delta with identity-cover topology, together with Tag 08QD (remark-simplicial-modules): L pi_! is the alternating-face complex, and degreewise flatness makes the module sheaf flat so its ordinary tensor represents its derived tensor.

proof.text: Regard $R,S,M$ as ring and module presheaves on the small category $\Delta$, with topology generated by identity coverings. Every presheaf satisfies the sheaf condition: the matching family for an identity covering is exactly its one section. Thus sheafification is the identity. Module kernels and cokernels are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and tensor is sectionwise [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensoring any exact sequence with $M_n$ preserves exactness for every $n$. Consequently $M$ is a flat $R$-module sheaf in the exact-tensor sense [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The same reasoning applies to any presheaf whose values are flat modules.

For a simplicial $R$-module $K$, put $F_m=R[h_{[m]}]$, so $(F_m)_n=\bigoplus_{\alpha:[n]\to[m]}R_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module], each $x\in K_m$ defines a map $F_m\to K$, sending $e_\alpha(r)$ to $rK(\alpha)(x)$. The sum over all pairs $(m,x)$ gives a map $E(K)=\bigoplus_{m,x\in K_m}F_m\to K$. It is surjective in every degree: $y\in K_n$ is the image of $e_{\mathrm{id}_{[n]}}(1)$ in the summand indexed by $(n,y)$. All indexing sets are small in a universe containing the values of $K$. Set $K_0=M$, $E_p=E(K_p)$, $K_{p+1}=\ker(E_p\to K_p)$, and let $d:E_{p+1}\to E_p$ be the quotient to $K_{p+1}$ followed by its inclusion. Sectionwise image equals kernel and $d^2=0$, giving an exact augmented resolution $\cdots\to E_1\to E_0\to M\to0$ by simplicial modules. Each $(E_p)_n$ is free over $R_n$, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], so each $E_p$ is flat by Step 1.

source.place: Tag 08RX, proof, reduction to sums of j_U! O_U; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EW (lemma-module-quotient-flat), explicit section-indexed surjection and its iteration

proof.text:
The sequences $0\to K_{p+1}\to E_p\to K_p\to0$ are short exact $R$-module sheaf sequences on the identity-cover site. Starting with flat $K_0=M$ and flat $E_p$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses] proves inductively that every $K_{p+1}$ is flat. Its tensor-exactness clause, applied with the $R$-module sheaf underlying $S$, gives short exact sequences
$$0\to K_{p+1}\otimes_RS\to E_p\otimes_RS\to K_p\otimes_RS\to0.$$
Splicing these sequences shows that $E_\bullet\otimes_RS\to M\otimes_RS$ remains an exact augmented resolution, sectionwise. This uses flatness of the quotients $K_p$, not flatness of $S$ or of the ring map $R\to S$.

source.place: sites-modules.tex Tags 03EX (lemma-flat-tor-zero), 03EY (lemma-flat-ses); the ordinary-tensor realization of the flat case in 08RX

proof.text: For a generator $F_m$, extension of scalars identifies $F_m\otimes_RS$ with $S[h_{[m]}]$: in degree $n$, the map sends $e_\alpha(r)\otimes t$ to $e_\alpha(f_n(r)t)$, with inverse $e_\alpha(t)\mapsto e_\alpha(1)\otimes t$. The composites are identities because $e_\alpha(r)\otimes t=e_\alpha(1)\otimes f_n(r)t$ by balancing, and $f_n(1)t=t$. The same formula works for any direct sum of generators because each element has finite support. For $\varphi:[k]\to[n]$, both orders of this identification and restriction send $e_\alpha(r)\otimes t$ to $e_{\alpha\varphi}(f_k(R(\varphi)(r))S(\varphi)(t))$, by naturality of $f$. Thus these are identifications of simplicial modules and identify the canonical map $F_m\to F_m\otimes_RS$ with $e_\alpha(r)\mapsto e_\alpha(f_n(r))$.

source.place: Tag 08RX, proof, the explicit X_bullet and X_prime_bullet models

proof.text: The underlying simplicial abelian groups of $R[h_{[m]}]$ and $S[h_{[m]}]$ are $P_m(R)$ and $P_m(S)$ of [lem-sfb-simplicial-simplex-copower-contraction]. The square with top map $s(P_m(f))$, bottom map $s(f)$, and vertical augmentations $s(\varepsilon_R),s(\varepsilon_S)$ commutes: on $e_\alpha(r)$ either composite gives $f_n(r)$. The cited node makes both vertical arrows invertible in $D(\mathrm{Ab})$, while $s(f)$ is invertible by hypothesis. Hence in $D(\mathrm{Ab})$ the top arrow equals $s(\varepsilon_S)^{-1}s(f)s(\varepsilon_R)$, a composite of invertible arrows, so it is invertible. Applying each cohomology functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to this invertible arrow makes its cohomology map invertible. This proves the required quasi-isomorphism for every free representable generator, without assuming that the maps $f_n$ are isomorphisms or flat.

source.place: Tag 08RX, proof, final homotopy-equivalence square; simplicial.tex Tags 08Q3 and 019S

proof.text: Since each $E_p$ is a sum of these generators, Step 5 implies that $u_p:s(E_p)\to s(E_p\otimes_RS)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Indeed the alternating-face differential preserves each generator summand. Its kernel is the sum of the summand kernels, since every element has finite support. Its image is the sum of the summand images: a finite tuple of boundaries admits a finite tuple of primitives. Passing to kernel modulo image therefore identifies homology with the sum of the summand homologies, and identifies $H(u_p)$ with the sum of the generator isomorphisms. The inverse is their coordinatewise inverse; it preserves finite support. Thus it is an isomorphism even for an empty set of generators.

source.place: Tag 08RX, proof, passage from j_U! O_U to direct sums

proof.text: Form the homological double complexes of abelian groups $A_{p,n}=(E_p)_n$ and $B_{p,n}=(E_p\otimes_RS)_n$ for $p,n\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-double-complex], with first index the resolution degree $p$ and second index the simplicial degree $n$. The resolution and alternating-face differentials commute because every resolution map is simplicial. Let $T_A^{-k}=\bigoplus_{p+n=k}A_{p,n}$, with differential $d_{\rm res}+(-1)^p d_{\rm face}$, and similarly $T_B$. Each sum is finite, and the two cross terms cancel, as in [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] in the abelian category $\mathrm{Ab}^{\rm op}$: reversing arrows turns our double complexes into first-quadrant cochain double complexes with the same indices, kernels and cokernels exchange, so quasi-isomorphisms correspond, and finite total sums are the finite total products. For a map $A\to B$ the reversed map is $B^{\rm op}\to A^{\rm op}$; the hypothesis on its complexes reverses with it, and the total comparison it gives reverses back to the displayed homological total map $T_A\to T_B$. Its hypothesis concerns, for each fixed second index $n$, the complexes in the first index $p$. Let $M^{(0)}$ be the double complex with $M_n$ in bidegree $(0,n)$, zero elsewhere, and face differential; its total complex is $s(M)$. The augmentation $E_0\to M$, zero for $p>0$, is a double-complex map $A\to M^{(0)}$: $\varepsilon d_{\rm res}=0$ since $E_1\to E_0\to M$ is zero, and $\varepsilon$ commutes with every face. For fixed $n$ it is $(E_\bullet)_n\to M_n$ in degree zero; by Steps 2 and 3 the resolution homology of $A$ and $B$ vanishes in positive degrees, and the augmentations induce the quotient isomorphisms $A_{0,n}/\operatorname{im}d\cong M_n$ and $B_{0,n}/\operatorname{im}d\cong(M\otimes_RS)_n$. So $A\to M^{(0)}$ and $B\to(M\otimes_RS)^{(0)}$ satisfy the hypothesis, and the augmentations $a:T_A\to s(M)$ and $b:T_B\to s(M\otimes_RS)$ are quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08RX, proof, passage through a bounded-above resolution; homology.tex Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), dual finite-diagonal comparison

proof.text: The maps $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ on $E_p$ give a double-complex map $\Phi:A\to B$: scalar extension sends the resolution differential to $d\otimes1$, so $(d\otimes1)(x\otimes1)=d(x)\otimes1$, and a simplicial operator sends $x\otimes1$ to $E_p(\varphi)(x)\otimes S(\varphi)(1)=E_p(\varphi)(x)\otimes1$. For fixed $p$ its complex in $n$ is $u_p$, a quasi-isomorphism by Step 6. Transpose: $A^t_{n,p}=A_{p,n}$, with simplicial index first, so its signed total has differential $d_{\rm face}+(-1)^nd_{\rm res}$. Let $\sigma$ multiply bidegree $(p,n)$ by $(-1)^{pn}$. For $x\in A_{p,n}$, $\sigma(d x)=(-1)^{(p-1)n}d_{\rm res}x+(-1)^{p+p(n-1)}d_{\rm face}x=(-1)^{pn}\big(d_{\rm face}x+(-1)^nd_{\rm res}x\big)=d^t(\sigma x)$, so $\sigma:T_A\to\operatorname{Tot}(A^t)$ is an isomorphism of complexes. It is natural in $\Phi$, and likewise for $B$. The complexes of $A^t$ with fixed second index $p$ are the columns $s(E_p)$, and $\Phi^t$ restricts there to $u_p$. Hence [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison], applied in $\mathrm{Ab}^{\rm op}$ as in Step 7, makes $\operatorname{Tot}(\Phi^t)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Conjugating by the two sign isomorphisms, $u:T_A\to T_B$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08RX, proof, comparison on generators extended through the resolution; homology.tex Tag 0133

proof.text: Let $v:s(M)\to s(M\otimes_RS)$ be the map of the statement. The augmentation square satisfies $bu=va$: on the $p=0$ summand its equality is $\varepsilon(x)\otimes1=(\varepsilon\otimes1)(x\otimes1)$, and both augmentations vanish on $p>0$. Thus $H(v)=H(b)H(u)H(a)^{-1}$ in every degree. Steps 7 and 8 make the three factors isomorphisms. Explicitly, $H(a)H(u)^{-1}H(b)^{-1}$ is a two-sided inverse to $H(v)$ by the displayed equality. Hence this particular canonical map $v$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
